PR #24 is deliberately reduced to typed settings, privacy admission, portable receipts and history-fenced mutations. Fresh swarm close delegates to native close. Any journal replay refuses `swarm_close_recovery_unsupported`; there is no automatic close repair or restore.

This Feature owns the deferred recovery protocol and all close blockers from review rounds 5–15:

- Resolve every short or full item ID through the exact host-bound native `get()` before selecting a history stream, including service-capable and installed-extension layouts. Capture the native history head before the authoritative document read and compare it under the same writer lock as every write.
- Identify each own forward close and restore through a unique durable `compensation_id`, the validated SDK transaction identity, exact mutation target and native receipt. Author equality, copied message markers, matching documents and matching fencing tokens are never ownership proof. An unrelated same-author native close must never be adopted.
- Delegate lifecycle policy to native close: dependent auto-unblock, blocker-field removal, Plan behavior and native warnings. Derive successors from actual native read-back; preserve unavailable warning/result receipts honestly.
- Persist the immutable complete member list, pre-close byte digests and post-close history heads before the first restore. Persist every own restore identity and durable restored/pending progress; fsync journal and directory updates through one coordinator.
- Resume own progress after a lost return or SIGKILL without treating it as a peer history advance. Skip only certified completed members. Keep item bytes correct while retaining append-only audit history.
- Compensate the entire native lifecycle domain after ordinary failures; never reopen a blocker while its dependents remain unblocked unintentionally. Foreign or peer edits stop recovery with typed partial receipts listing restored and pending members.
- Recheck monotonic native history under the writer lock for close, release, restore, rollback and recovery. Preserve release/claim/restore ABA even when the final bytes and token are identical, including peer changes after preflight and after a decision read.
- A real-process SIGKILL harness interrupts every forward and reverse boundary, including after each restore 0..N with 1–3 dependents. Recovery must converge without duplicates or loss to exact pre-close item bytes, retaining audit history. Inject peer edits between every restore and copied identities in later same-author mutations.
- Never mix SDK runtime copies for locking or mutation scopes. Test shared/separate installed SDK layouts, non-Git trackers, actual packed npm/Bun consumers and complete documents/history messages passing privacy admission.
- Every regression must fail with its fix reverted. Keep both privacy refusal and benign corpora. Achieve unchanged 100/100/100/100 coverage and complete release gates, with documentation and remedies.

Tracked by [pm-swarm-durable-close-recovery](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/main/.agents/pm/features/pm-swarm-durable-close-recovery.toon), related to [pm-swarm-y972](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/main/.agents/pm/features/pm-swarm-y972.toon). Existing issue #32 is the narrower dependent-progress subtask.

The retired prototype and tests remain available at commit `0157465` for reproduction; they are not part of the reduced implementation. This is package implementation work, not a new SDK-gap claim.
